To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

1) the distribution of V2axons and synapses in larval zebraﬁsh spinal cord is topographically ordered, and 2) dorsal V2a neurons, which are recruited earlier in swimming, project farther than ventral ones, and have higher proximal synapse densities.

the morphology of spinal premotor interneuron V2a cells is differentially distributed across the dorsoventra axis, with more dorsal V2a axon terminals having longer projections than more ventral V2a axonic terminations.

(a) the morphology of spinal cord V2a neurons changes systematically with their recruitment order during increases in swimming speed, (b) V2a cells project axons to more dorsal spinal cord locations, and (c) the number of synapses on V2a neurons increases with their recruitment order, and the synapses are more proximally located.
